topic: The Borsuk-Ulam Theorem and the Stolen Necklace Problem
target_audience: Undergraduate students in mathematics or computer science

sections.title: Intuitive Prerequisite: The Antipodal Mapping
lecture_lines: Consider a sphere, the surface S².
They sit exactly opposite each other.
animations: Draw a sphere in #FFFFFF. Label 'S²' in #00FF00.
Mark a point 'x' in #FF0000 on the sphere.
Mark the antipodal point '-x' in #0000FF opposite 'x'.
Connect 'x' and '-x' with a dashed line through center.
Flash 'x' and '-x' to emphasize they are antipodal.

sections.title: The Borsuk-Ulam Theorem
lecture_lines: Any continuous function maps some antipodal pair.
Think of temperature on Earth's surface.
animations: Show a globe with a temperature gradient in #FFFF00.
Identify antipodal points P1 and P2 on the globe.
Display two identical thermometers showing same value in #FF0000.
Show the Borsuk-Ulam theorem text: 'f(x) = f(-x)'.
Highlight the points P1, P2 moving across the globe surface.

sections.title: Transition: The Necklace Problem
lecture_lines: Thieves must divide a beaded necklace.
Each needs half of every bead type.
This is the discrete necklace problem.
animations: Draw a string of beads with 10 red (in #FF0000) and 10 blue (in #0000FF).
Draw two separate piles for Thief A and Thief B.
Animate cutting the string at two random points.
Show redistribution of segments into the two piles.
Final state: each pile has 5 red and 5 blue.

sections.title: The Mathematical Bridge
lecture_lines: We map discrete cuts to a sphere.
Fair division becomes a zero-sum function.
Borsuk-Ulam guarantees an exact fair solution.
animations: Show the necklace string transforming into a circular loop.
Map the loop onto the surface of a 2D sphere.
Identify cut configurations as coordinates (x, y, z) on sphere.
Visualize the function value crossing zero as the cuts shift.
Highlight the intersection point as the fair division solution.

sections.title: Conclusion and Application
lecture_lines: Topology solves complex resource sharing problems.
Curvature of space ensures perfect fairness.
animations: Draw the final balanced piles: 5 red/5 blue in each.
Show Alice and Bob smiling, representing fair distribution.
Flash the scissors icon as the tool for division.
Overlay: 'Fair division is mathematically guaranteed'.
Fade everything out slowly to black (#000000).
